correctness.rationale: For all \(s=p^f\), the partial derivatives prove smoothness and direct norm/trace give exactly one \(\mathbb F_q\)-point. The shift \(c^s+c=-\eta\) has \(q\)-Frobenius displacement \(\delta=\eta-\eta^s\), an order-\(p\) Hermitian elation. Over \(\mathbb F_q\), its nontrivial powers are conjugate by norm-scaling diagonal automorphisms. Hermitian maximality gives every Frobenius eigenvalue \(-s\); restriction to character eigenspaces commutes with Frobenius and does not assume Jordan semisimplicity. The base-field trace forces \(\operatorname{Tr}(U^j)=-s\), cyclic character inversion yields multiplicities \(s^2/p-s\) and \(s^2/p\); full polynomial and counts follow by Weil trace for every \(n\). Independent exhaustive small-field checks over \(\mathbb F_4,\mathbb F_{16},\mathbb F_9,\mathbb F_{81}\) yield \((1,9,1,109)\). No asymptotic or finite enumeration is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The Hasse–Weil numerator is a natural intrinsic invariant. The result resolves it for the complete infinite one-point family across all prime powers, all non-subfield parameters, and all extension degrees, identifying a hidden characteristic-p descent spectrum. Neither a base-field one-point count nor an arbitrary roots-of-unity congruence determines this polynomial, and the precision is relevant to arithmetic geometry and finite-field curve codes. It is not an arbitrary small example, routine table increment, or a stand-alone necessary-condition check.
